content:
iOS 26.6 will be released to iPhone users next week, and Apple's release notes have clearly informed us about the contents of this software update.

iOS 26.6 optimizes the Spotlight search function for the iOS 27 upgrade, and includes security fixes and bug fixes

Earlier this week, Apple released the RC (Release Candidate) version of iOS 26.6 to developers and public beta users. In other words, the public release is imminent.

iOS 26.6 is expected to officially launch early next week, alongside companion updates such as macOS Tahoe 26.6. It could arrive as early as Monday, July 27.

These updates are not focused on adding new features, but are dedicated to making iOS 26 more stable, secure, and bug-free, while preparing iPhones for the upgrade to iOS 27.

Below are Apple's official release notes:

Apple will announce specific security update content when the software officially launches next week. Among the most noteworthy details are those involving the Spotlight indexing feature.

iOS 27 will debut this autumn and will feature a comprehensive redesign of the Spotlight search function. To align with the related changes, iOS 26.6 will be the first to begin optimizing Spotlight indexing on iPhone.

When the first iOS 27 developer beta was released, testers found that Spotlight took a very long time to build its index—potentially up to a week or even longer. By pre-launching the related process in iOS 26.6, users will enjoy a smoother initial experience when iOS 27 rolls out.

In addition to the above changes, iOS 26.6 also introduces a new alert feature that notifies users when they have reached the limit on the number of blocked contacts, and includes a new anti-theft feature code, which may only officially launch later.

How has iOS 26 performed so far? Are there any bugs still waiting for Apple to fix? Feel free to let us know in the comments section.
